clue.text: Thought it would turn up in time

indicators.note: in says the reversed word sits inside the word for time

parts.note: noon is a time of day

indicators.note: turn up says the word it is flipped round, read the other way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone trusts that an idea will occur to them eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion is an idea or belief, something one has thought.

clue.text: In use, can turn into a problem

indicators.note: turn says the letters of the words before it change their order

explanation.surface: Something in service can become troublesome.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuisance is an annoyance or trouble.

clue.text: Learnt to change and accept things

definitions.note: verb phrase standing for the adjective meaning willing to accept things

indicators.note: change says the letters of the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has learnt to adapt and go along with life.
explanation.definitionFit: A tolerant person puts up with what others do.

clue.text: Work in musical drama causes a twitch after a long time

indicators.note: after says the twitch is placed following the long time

parts.note: OP, opus, is a musical work
an era is a long period
a tic is a nervous twitch

explanation.surface: A piece of music theatre makes someone twitch after ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Operatic means relating to or as in opera, a drama set to music.

clue.text: Crazy for something to eat

explanation.surface: Mad about a snack.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackers is slang for mad, and crackers are dry biscuits eaten with cheese.

clue.text: Order great changes when going back

indicators.note: changes says the letters of the words before it are reordered

explanation.surface: Big reforms are made when reversing.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrograde means moving backwards.

clue.text: Cricketer reaches it to end about right

indicators.note: about says the word for end wraps round the letter

parts.note: to cease is to end

explanation.surface: A batsman makes ground before stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the crease is the line a batsman must reach to complete a run or avoid being out.
explanation.definitionFit: The crease is the marked line at the wicket that a batsman stretches for.

clue.text: Divorcee uses the back room in Devon

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse

indicators.note: the back says the word room is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A former spouse lives in the rear room of a Devon home.
explanation.walkthrough: Exmoor is a moorland national park in south-west England, partly in the county of Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: Exmoor is moorland lying in Devon and Somerset.

clue.text: It is certain that a river runs through a farm building

definitions.note: a sentence standing for the noun meaning certainty

indicators.note: runs through says the river goes inside the building

parts.note: a sty is a pigs' building on a farm
the Ure is a Yorkshire river

explanation.surface: A stream definitely flows past a pigpen.
explanation.definitionFit: Surety is certainty, as in the old phrase of a surety.

clue.text: Some plain lie, unlikely to have taken place

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A blatant falsehood is told about something that probably never happened.
explanation.definitionFit: In lieu means instead of, which fits 'to have taken place' read as having taken the place of something.

clue.text: A bad cold might produce a headline

definitions.text: A bad cold might produce a headline

parts.words: A bad cold might produce a headline
parts.note: a heavy cold makes the nose run, so one suffering is someone who streams; a newspaper banner headline running across the page has the same name

explanation.surface: A heavy cold sets the newspapers buzzing.
explanation.definitionFit: A banner headline across the whole width of a newspaper page is called by this name, as is someone with a runny nose.

clue.text: Sailor on the way to another country

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
a road is a way

explanation.surface: A seaman sets off on the route overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Going abroad means travelling to a foreign land.

clue.text: Not long enough for the itchy torso to get hot

indicators.note: itchy suggests restless squirming, so these letters are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A garment fails to cover an itching chest, making it warm.
explanation.definitionFit: Something too short falls below the required length.

clue.text: Wandering newsman came back in — a close call!

indicators.note: in says the reversed piece goes inside the pair of words

parts.note: close as in stingy means mean
to ring is to call by telephone

indicators.note: came back says the word for newsman is turned round

parts.note: ED, editor, is a newsman

explanation.surface: A roving reporter returns after a narrow escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'came back' turns ED into DE, which goes inside MEAN and RING; 'a close call' looks like one phrase but splits into close (mean) and call (ring).
explanation.definitionFit: Meandering means winding about aimlessly, like wandering.

clue.text: Measurement of time in the middle

indicators.note: in says one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: the centre is the middle
taken as written

explanation.surface: A measure taken of time at its midpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: A centimetre is a metric unit of length, so a measurement.

clue.text: One hundred first class acts, but they cause back problem

indicators.note: cause loosely signals that these pieces bring about a new arrangement of their letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
A1 means first class, written AI

explanation.surface: A hundred top-rate performances give someone a bad back.
explanation.definitionFit: Sciatica is pain from the sciatic nerve running down the lower back and leg.

clue.text: Governing who gets put up around Ireland

indicators.note: around says the reversed word goes round the name for Ireland
put up in a down clue says the word gets is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Erin is a poetic name for Ireland

explanation.surface: Ruling on who is accommodated near Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Steering is directing or controlling, as in governing.

clue.text: Perhaps he resolved a dispute that DJ argued about

indicators.note: about says the letters of the words before it are shuffled around

explanation.surface: A disc jockey quarrelled and someone stepped in to settle it.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjudger is one who judges or decides between parties.

clue.text: One foreign antique coin for the journalist who doesn't know much

parts.note: une is French for one (feminine)
a ducat is an old gold coin of Europe
ED, editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A foreign old coin is handed to an ignorant reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: UNE is the feminine form of the French for one; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An uneducated person has had little schooling and knows little.

clue.text: Do return after journey made in three legs!

indicators.note: after says the reversed word comes following the journey

parts.note: a trip is a journey

indicators.note: return says the word do is turned back

explanation.surface: Someone does a trip again and runs a three-legged race.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripod is a stand with three legs.

clue.text: Get above the teacher

explanation.surface: Rise above the schoolmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: To master is to get the better of; a master is a schoolteacher.

clue.text: Scale of the party for engineers on the road

parts.note: a do is a party
RE is the Royal Engineers
M1 is the London-to-Yorkshire motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: A party of road engineers takes the measure of things.
explanation.definitionFit: Do, re, mi are the first notes of the sol-fa musical scale.

clue.text: Understood about lad (Oriental) who argued

indicators.note: about says the first word wraps round the others

parts.note: to read a situation is to understand it
a son is a lad
E stands for East, the Orient

explanation.surface: An Eastern boy who debated was grasped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like RE, but it wraps READ round SON and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To have reasoned is to have put a case logically, like arguing.

clue.text: French composer who hit the water

parts.note: to ram is to strike
eau is French for water

explanation.surface: A Frenchman who wrote music struck the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Philippe Rameau was an eighteenth-century French composer of operas.

clue.text: Lamentable way to send back a quote

parts.note: a path is a way

indicators.note: to send back says the word for quote is turned round

parts.note: to cite is to quote

explanation.surface: A sad method of returning a citation.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathetic means pitiful or woefully inadequate.

clue.text: Criminal goes into it to avoid being given one!

definitions.text: Criminal goes into it to avoid being given one!

parts.words: Criminal goes into it to avoid being given one!
parts.note: a criminal lies low to escape, and in doing so escapes a thrashing: one word means both concealment and a beating

explanation.surface: A crook vanishes to dodge punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both concealment and, in British slang, a thrashing.

clue.text: Peter Pan's friends were precious

explanation.surface: The boy who never grew up had beloved companions.
explanation.definitionFit: The Darling children, Wendy, John and Michael, fly with Peter Pan; and darlings are dear, precious ones.

clue.text: Hazard of digging the garden

indicators.note: digging turns soil over, so these letters are turned over into a new order

explanation.surface: A risk that comes with gardening.
explanation.definitionFit: A danger is a hazard, a source of peril.
